newsitem.title: UK: Russian straight run lurks over NWE cracked market.
newsitem.headline: Russian straight run lurks over NWE cracked market.

text.p: High sulphur cracked fuel oil barges dipped and then recovered on Wednesday, the market knocked lower by overhanging Russian straight run fuel and some pressure to push barges lower for pricing purposes.
Trades were recorded in a band between $105-109 fob ARA a tonne with the market settling towards the upper end.
Low sulphur barges were pegged a touch higher around $120 fob a tonne, although no deals were heard.
High sulphur cracked fuel was poised steady around $110-112 cif NWE despite a deal done yesterday at $120.50 cif Brindisi for 33,000 tonnes out of NWE.
"The Med does look to be a touch firmer than the north, but perhaps not as high as that," said one trader.
A NWE end-user was thought to have bought a high water content Russian straight run cargo at around $106-107 cif.
"Its still tight on the cracked side, but prices have not been able to move higher because of the presence of straight run," commented one trader.
Low sulphur cracked cargoes were steady at around $117-118 fob NWE while offers into the Med were close to a $127-129 cif Med range.
